data.body:
Correction after experimental root-cause proof and production recovery (2026-07-28):

The earlier Phase 1 account correctly described why an artifact failure could persist, but it did not identify the initiating persistence failure. Real two-clone experiments isolated that cause. Enrichment queue pruning physically deleted committed ENQUEUE_ENRICH, CLAIM_ENRICH, and DONE_ENRICH events; digest keep=1 pruning physically deleted committed TICKET_DIGEST events. Queue deletion alone reproduced stale-clone merge conflicts on DONE_ENRICH. Digest deletion alone reproduced conflicts on TICKET_DIGEST. With both deletion paths disabled, the same independently advancing clones merged cleanly and retained the union of both histories. Production recovery then reproduced exactly two DONE_ENRICH rename/delete conflicts at the frozen divergent tips. Therefore destructive event deletion created the unreconcilable tracker divergence; vote/dedup retry suppression was only an amplifier that prevented self-healing after persistence failed.

Recovery preserved and republished the original revision artifact 8172-4554-a9fc-47da. After the repair deployed and the tracker reconverged, a forced rerun of Gerrit change 986 created fresh shared artifact a4b7-f176-50af-49aa with schema code_review_result_v2 and a relates_to link from work ticket 9447-b31c-e0b7-446d. The tracker remained clean and 0 ahead / 0 behind.

This ticket remains open: revision d51c056d0b4859d1a5fcb311b311c4e531919078 now has two revision-scoped artifacts (8172-4554-a9fc-47da and a4b7-f176-50af-49aa), so the acceptance criterion requiring exactly one idempotent artifact is not yet met. Resolving that duplicate/idempotency defect remains in this ticket scope.
